title: Extra 330LT (cockpit)
intro: The Extra 330LT is an aerobatic aeroplane built for stunt flying. The cockpit is small and simple: a centre stick, rudder pedals, a compact panel with one big Garmin G3X screen and a few backup instruments, and a quadrant of three levers on the left side for the throttle, the propeller and the mixture.

sources.title: Extra 330LT (public knowledge: aerobatic single-seat cockpit, Garmin G3X)
JoyPro function tables MSFS2020/2024 and X-Plane 11/12 (DB/Functions)

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: A compact panel with one large screen and a few backup instruments.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: A compact aerobatic panel with the Garmin G3X display, a G-meter, backup speed and height gauges, the magneto and starter switch and the electrical switches.
panels.context: The pilot flies mostly by looking outside. The panel shows the speed, the height, the engine data and how hard the aircraft is pulled in turns.

controls.name: Garmin G3X display
controls.text: This large screen shows the flight data (attitude, speed, height) and the engine data. It replaces many round gauges.
controls.context: It is the main instrument of the panel.

controls.name: G-meter
controls.text: This gauge shows the load factor, in G. It shows how hard the pilot is pushed into the seat during turns and pull-ups.
controls.context: In aerobatics, the pilot watches it to stay within the limits of the aircraft and of the pilot.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: A backup gauge that shows how fast the aircraft moves through the air.
controls.context: It is used if the screen fails and as a cross-check.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: A backup gauge that shows the height above sea level.
controls.context: It is used if the screen fails and as a cross-check.

controls.name: Magneto / starter switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The magnetos are off and the engine stops.

positions.name: R
positions.text: Only the right magneto gives sparks.

positions.name: L
positions.text: Only the left magneto gives sparks.

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: Both magnetos work, the normal setting.

positions.name: START
positions.text: The starter turns the engine. It springs back to BOTH on release.

controls.text: This switch turns on the magnetos (the sparks of the engine) and the starter. The pilot turns it to START to crank the engine, then it springs back to BOTH.
controls.context: It works like the ignition key of a car, but the engine has two magnetos for safety.

controls.name: Master and avionics switches
controls.text: These switches connect the battery to the aircraft and give power to the screen and the radios (avionics).
controls.context: The pilot switches the master on first.

areas.name: Left side: engine levers and trim
areas.text: The levers on the left side of the cockpit for the engine, the trim and the fuel.

panels.name: Left side console
panels.text: The quadrant on the left side with the throttle, propeller and mixture levers, the elevator trim lever and the fuel selector or pump.
panels.context: The pilot handles the engine and the trim with the left hand.

controls.name: Throttle lever
controls.text: This lever controls the engine power. Moving it forward gives more power.
controls.context: The pilot pushes it forward for take-off and pulls it back for landing.

controls.name: Propeller lever
controls.text: This lever sets how fast the propeller turns. The engine has a propeller that changes its pitch (how sharply the blades bite the air).
controls.context: The pilot sets a high speed for take-off and a lower one for cruise.

controls.name: Mixture lever
controls.text: This lever sets the fuel and air mixture from rich to lean. Fully back stops the engine.
controls.context: The pilot leans the mixture at high altitude.

controls.name: Elevator trim lever
controls.text: This small lever trims the elevator, the flap on the tail that pitches the nose. It takes the force from the stick.
controls.context: The pilot trims whenever the speed changes.

controls.name: Fuel selector / pump
controls.text: This control chooses the fuel tank and works the fuel pump.
controls.context: The pilot sets it for the start and changes it in flight when needed.

areas.name: Stick, levers and pedals
areas.text: The controls that match your joystick, throttle and pedals.

panels.name: Control stick
panels.text: The centre stick between the pilot's knees.
panels.context: The pilot flies by moving the stick.

controls.name: Control stick
controls.text: Pushing the stick forward and pulling it back moves the elevator and pitches the nose down and up. Moving it sideways rolls the aircraft.
controls.context: It is the main control for flying by hand and for aerobatics.

panels.name: Engine levers and trim
panels.text: The throttle, propeller and mixture levers on the left side and the trim lever, as they match a throttle device.
panels.context: The pilot handles them with the left hand.

controls.name: Throttle
controls.text: The throttle lever on the left side. Moving it forward gives more engine power.
controls.context: On a throttle device this is the first of three lever axes.

controls.name: Propeller
controls.text: The lever beside the throttle. It sets the speed of the propeller.
controls.context: On a throttle device this is the second of three lever axes.

controls.name: Mixture
controls.text: The lever beside the propeller lever. It sets the mixture from rich to cut-off.
controls.context: On a throttle device this is the third lever axis.

controls.name: Elevator trim lever
controls.text: The small lever on the left side. Moving it forward trims the nose down, aft trims the nose up.
controls.context: Trim takes the force off the stick.

panels.name: Rudder pedals
panels.text: The rudder pedals at the pilot's feet with the toe brakes on top.
panels.context: They steer the aircraft in the air and on the ground.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: The pedals move the rudder left and right. The toe brakes on top of the pedals brake the left and right wheels.
controls.context: The pedals keep the aircraft straight and are used in aerobatic figures.
